content.text: "Osteoporosis is thinning and weakening of bones and affects all of us as we age involving both men and women," revealed Dr Mirza Rehman Beg, Associate Professor and Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Osteoporosis - The Silent Bone Killer" at 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' monthly health awareness programme held on May 13, 2000.

Dr Beg informed that it is a universal problem,"In 1990, 1.6 million fractures occurred in United Stated and Europe requiring surgery. Figures in Pakistan should be comparable or perhaps more because of lack of awareness in our population and poor nutritional status especially in our urban population. Although this condition is preventable and treatable yet it goes unrecognized and untreated due to lack of awareness in the public and in many general physicians."

Dr Beg further added that,"as we grow older our bones lose their density and become weaker but certain factors can accelerate this process to the extent that some bones like hip and wrist fracture require operation. Simple movements such as coughing, sneezing, weight lifting, etc. can lead to vertebral (backbone) fracture. The accelerating factors for osteoporosis are mainly dietary deficiency of calcium, vitamin and minerals.

Menopause in women, which drops the estrogen hormone level, these women require hormone replacement therapy in-addition to calcium, vitamin and minerals. Lack of exercises especially in urban population will accelerate osteoporosis. Smoking and alcohol usage also accelerates osteoporosis."
Dr Beg concluded by saying that,"Osteoporosis is preventable by diet and exercise, HRT in women who have had menopause and early' recognition and treatment."
